items.title: Switching languages can change a chatbot's personality test results
items.excerpt: USTC researchers gave five chatbots Big Five personality questionnaires in English and Mandarin (one also in French); answers held steady within a language but trait scores shifted in model-specific directions when the language changed.

items.title: LLMs show a human-like double standard when judging others' reasoning
items.excerpt: Harvard researchers found GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet produce Bayes-consistent probability estimates yet judge a hypothetical person reasoning the same way more harshly than human participants do.

items.title: AI agents develop their own 'artificial natural language' to communicate about complex data
items.excerpt: Researchers in Brussels and Namur show autonomous agents can build a shared, interpretable communication system grounded in their own sensor data, tested on 37 datasets from wine chemistry to exoplanets.

items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.excerpt: Caltech, CU Boulder and NVIDIA researchers used a recurrent neural operator to forecast tipping points, predicting the loss of ocean low clouds in simulation more than two years ahead with about an 11-day timing error.

items.title: Forecasting air drag with deep learning helps predict when uncontrolled satellites and rocket stages fall to Earth
items.excerpt: A hybrid of Newtonian orbital mechanics and a neural network that learns how an object's ballistic coefficient changes over time, trained on 11 years of tracking data, kept reentry predictions within their uncertainty windows.

items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.excerpt: Google Research built VERID, a live digital twin of a robotic wet-lab workcell that lets AI agents simulate and safety-check liquid-handling protocols, and ran closed-loop agent experiments that improved aptamer hit rates and yielded nanomolar de novo protein binders.

items.title: Google Antigravity: Accelerating antimicrobial peptide search
items.excerpt: Biologists used DeepMind's Antigravity agentic platform with the ProtNLM protein-function model to surface a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate, now entering wet-lab validation.

items.title: Riverlane and NVIDIA use AI to speed up quantum decoder calibration
items.excerpt: Riverlane and NVIDIA are testing AI and GPU acceleration to speed up quantum error-correction decoder calibration as quantum hardware behaviour drifts.

items.title: FirstQFM model cuts single-qubit gate times by 33% on QuantWare processor
items.excerpt: FirstQFM applied its quantum foundation model to a QuantWare superconducting QPU, shortening single-qubit gate times and improving Bell-state fidelity on five qubit pairs.

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: A study finds people draw a sharp line between human and AI consciousness even when both behave identically, rating the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human.

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to map nearly 10,000 reactions in CO2-to-fuel conversion, uncovering pathways traditional models missed and sharply improving predictions of CO2 reduction.

items.title: Physicists develop early warning system that predicts when an AI is about to go rogue
items.excerpt: A physics-derived formula tracks an AI model's internal 'compass needle' to flag undesirable outputs before they are generated.

items.title: Claude just found a CRISPR-like DNA pattern, but even Anthropic's scientists aren't sure what it does
items.excerpt: The large language model took less than a day to identify a curious repeated stretch of DNA resembling CRISPR arrays; its function remains unknown.

items.title: OpenAI's blockbuster Navier-Stokes proof isn't what we thought it was
items.excerpt: Rumors that OpenAI's AI-generated 'Navier-Stokes' result lifted the work of two mathematicians may have been overblown, but the episode exposes how AI math claims get verified.

items.title: Danaher, Nvidia combine lab instrumentation and AI to advance autonomous science
items.excerpt: Danaher and Nvidia are pairing lab instruments with AI to push toward autonomous, self-driving experimentation in life-science labs.

items.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
items.excerpt: A citizen-science project asks volunteers to comb NASA telescope data for hidden black holes, because AI classifiers struggle with stellar flares and pulsations in the light curves.

items.title: Giving AI a 'crystal clear' view of the materials world
items.excerpt: MIT researchers built an AI model that pairs 3D atomic structures with natural-language descriptions from papers and databases to identify optimal crystalline materials for target applications.

items.title: KAIST robotic light-driven platform synthesizes new drug candidates in 24 hours
items.excerpt: KAIST built an unmanned continuous-flow platform where AI-designed molecules are made by robots using light-driven single-atom editing, producing N-methyl pyrrole scaffolds around the clock.

items.title: AI-generated fake mantis photo on iNaturalist alarms scientists
items.excerpt: An AI-generated mantis image posted to iNaturalist has citizen-science platforms racing to filter synthetic imagery before it contaminates biodiversity research data.

items.title: History's long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI
items.excerpt: Cryptographers' inboxes are flooding with requests to validate historical cipher solutions produced by amateurs working with AI tools.
